note: One artifact, one writer. On TP1-13797 the ticket probe wrote its receipt into `source-inventory.json` - the file it was supposed to be adding to - and erased the sources the scout had collected. Nothing refused it, because nothing anywhere said who owns that file. This is that statement, and `test_artifact_writers.py` holds it: every artifact `stages.json` declares has an owner here, the owner exists, and a new artifact cannot be added without deciding whose it is. `machinery` names code that writes the same file as part of the owner's own mechanism (a controller projection, a reducer the owner calls) - it is not a second author, it is the same one. Anything else that needs something in the file asks the owner's command, or writes its own file.

qa-factory/local-tickets/.why: the text of a story no tracker holds; never edited, never deleted

pipeline.json.why: state and journal in one call; the controller refreshes its own projection of it

work/context-manifest.json.why: the scout's own artifact, validated on write
work/context-manifest.json.rewrite: Edit (the one field), after locating it with Grep -n
work/context-manifest.json.rewrite_cost: 4 whole rewrites plus 11 throwaway python patchers on TP1-13797, 37,222 tokens of call arguments; a point editor for this file is still owed (P17)

work/context-bundle.json.why: built and validated by code from the manifest

work/source-inventory.json.why: collect/peek/assess/inspect/accept-gap are its commands; a probe receipt goes to ticket-probe.json and never here (F8)

work/impl-diff.txt.why: written once from the MR or branch the person named

work/requirements-register.md.why: the register is the role's judgement; claim_projector.py copies the S3 planner's claims into it (a Register row, the ids entry and a `## Behaviour claims` row with origin S3-grounding) because the planner has no Bash and is not its writer: no role is added
work/requirements-register.md.rewrite: Edit (one line per requirement row; several Edit calls in one turn)
work/requirements-register.md.rewrite_cost: 26 whole rewrites of it on TP1-13797 cost 22,684 tokens of call arguments, every one of them re-read on each later turn of the dispatch

work/requirements-readiness.json.why: the same dispatch writes both; question_register.py adds a raised before/now question (`--raise`, the S4 exit, the S3 claim projector) under its answers lock

understanding.md.why: the brief the person reads at gate A
understanding.md.rewrite_cost: 20 whole rewrites on TP1-13797 cost 8,284 tokens of call arguments and reverted what earlier turns had put there

work/sizing.json.why: the arithmetic is code's; the role quotes it

work/test-plan.json.why: written by the role, validated on write; plan_row.py changes one row of it in place (--set, --add-row, --put-row). `read_by_section` is not a writer: it names the section map the pre-tool guard prints when the file is read whole (artifact_sections.KINDS)

work/grounding.yaml.why: the grounding table: rows, requirements and claims are the strategist's; code fills the index sections when the skeleton is built (each node that adds such a script names it in `machinery` in its own commit)

work/blast-radius.json.why: the blast-radius index of the implementation diff, built by code from git objects of the recorded commit; `ensure` is the one writer (the CLI and brief_pack are its callers), the table copies it and the strategist only reads it

work/user-path-failures.json.why: the full list of places of the code that swallow a failure (G2-14), written by code when the S2 brief is built; the tester only reads it and decides which place is on a user path

work/flow-requests.json.why: the requests of the flow's code (`requests[]`: method, url_template, source, path, line, also_at), written by code when the S3 brief is built (`write_requests`, the one writer; `read_requests` the one reader); the strategist plans a row that fails each and the S3 exit owes it

work/base-slice/.why: the text of the changed code as it was, read by code from git objects of a named base; the strategist only reads it, and the readers judge by recomputing it (`base_slice.collect`), never by these files

work/test-cases/critic-findings.md.why: the S4 critic's findings live beside the cases they review, one file per area and round; listed before the directory below so the designer's directory does not claim them

work/test-code/critic-findings.md.why: the S5 twin of the S4 findings file (handoffs/s5-critic-to-automator.yaml); listed before its neighbours so a directory key never claims it

state/story-case-links.json.why: pinning is deterministic bookkeeping, never a role's

work/automation-manifest.json.why: fragments are merged by code so two windows cannot overwrite each other

work/s5-plan.json.why: the plan for every case of S5 is the automator's decision (levels, shapes, consolidation); `s5_plan.py --init` writes only the skeleton (cases, S3 rows, Then clauses) and moves a stale plan to work/s5-plan.prev.json; a plan rework grows it in place (`s5_plan.refresh`: rows of new cases, current hashes); the critic and the windows only read it (`s5_plan.load`)

work/s5-plan-reviews.json.why: the receipt of the plan the critic judged, written by `s5_plan.stamp_review` at the critic's `finish` before the review is accepted: the critic copies no hash, and no role writes this file

work/probe-models/.why: the critic's model of a reading B, one file per instance, case and alternative; the probe copies it into its record

work/probes/alternative/.why: the verdict of a Then under its declared reading B; never a live receipt

work/probes/.why: a probe record is the tool's own receipt

work/probes/product/.why: the verdict of a product probe (intended_failure, survived, probe_defect, incomplete) is the tool's own record; a repeat is answered from it

evidence/diagnostic-*.json.why: the output of the failure analyst's ONE diagnostic run of a test without the asserts of the Thens behind its red one (`red_sandbox.py --diagnostic`) is the tool's own record: the analyst cites it from the triage row's `diagnostic` block and never writes it, and a repeat over the same test bytes is answered from it

work/run-report.json.why: reduced from immutable run blocks; never hand-written

work/evidence/.why: every writer here writes its OWN receipt file, never another's

work/triage.json.why: a verdict with evidence is the analyst's; s7_pretriage.py writes only the rows marked `source: code` (a manual check whose own record says what stopped it), never over an analyst row; s7_reorder.py finish writes only `carried_attempts` and `carried_by: s7_reorder` on the row that asked for a `reorder`, after the edit was a pure move and the repair run stayed red; s7_reorder.py mark_fixed (the `mark-fixed` mode) writes only `fix_result: fixed` on such a carried row, once the critic approved

work/s7-reorder/.why: the snapshot of the test file before an S7 reorder round (`s7_reorder.py start`) is the tool's own record: `finish` judges the edit against it, and no role writes it

work/bug-drafts/.why: a draft is not a bug; the reporter files it after gate B

project:bugs/.why: only after a gate B decision names the draft

work/review-debts.json.why: the windows that closed over a code-critic rejection at a spent repair limit; the driver calls ledger.write_review_debt at the person's answer, the ledger is the one reader

work/traceability.json.why: one row per requirement x case, generated

test-report.md.why: the scribe writes it; --close-gate-b appends the decision
test-report.md.rewrite: Edit (the section that changed; --close-gate-b appends the decision itself)
test-report.md.rewrite_cost: 5 whole rewrites on TP1-13797 cost 32,115 tokens of call arguments - the report is long, so a rewrite is the most expensive single call a role makes

work/handoffs/.why: the form is created by code, filled by the role (field by field, or through <dispatch>.values.yaml, which handoff_check.py applies and renames), repaired and checked by code

state/findings/<dispatch>-digest-notes.m.why: what a role wrote after the path line of its digest, kept whole (`file_notes`) so a finding in it reaches the conductor; the accepted digest names it as `notes: <path>`

work/digests/.why: the digest of every handoff the exit gate passed, filed under its dispatch id (`<id>.txt`; the role's own text beside it as `<id>.original.txt` when code mended the form); `story_step finish --digest -` reads it, no role writes it

retro.md.why: prose by the role over numbers code computed; `numbers` mode writes it by code alone

project:readiness.json.why: the probe writes its own result

work/proposals/.why: a proposal and its receipt belong to the executor

work/exploratory-findings.jsonl.why: the one append-only writer of the findings register (`append`); investigation.py (`project`, `close_gaps`) and investigation_probe.py (`record`) call it and never write the file

work/evidence/investigation/.why: the captures of an exploratory probe belong to the probe that took them; nothing else writes under this folder
